name: GitHub
description: Search repositories, issues, pull requests, and commits.

fields.name: token
fields.label: Personal access token
fields.helpText: A PAT is sent as a bearer token. Grant only the repository and organization permissions needed.

permissionsText: The remote GitHub MCP server accepts a valid bearer access token, including a personal access token. The default /readonly endpoint restricts the remote toolset to read operations. OAuth uses the server's preconfigured GitHub OAuth app; the callback does not perform OAuth protected-resource discovery.

steps: Create a fine-grained personal access token for only the repositories you need, with read-only contents, issues, and pull request permissions as appropriate, or configure the GitHub OAuth app on the backend.

Connect AI uses GitHub's remote /readonly MCP endpoint by default. Paste the token or authorize in the popup; credentials are encrypted and the connection is reported only after MCP initialization and tool discovery.

scopes: Repository or organization read permissions required by selected tools

name: Linear
description: Search issues and project information through a Linear MCP server.

fields.name: token
fields.label: Linear API key
fields.helpText: Use a key with Read permission only.

permissionsText: The standard endpoint can expose write tools; use the read-only endpoint or a read-only key for investigations.

steps: Create a Linear API key with Read permission.
Paste it here and test the connection.

name: Jira
description: Connect to a separately managed local Jira MCP server.
permissionsText: The local mcp-atlassian process and its Jira credentials must be configured separately; Connect AI does not receive them.

steps: Start your configured Jira MCP server.
Use an endpoint reachable from the Connect AI backend.

name: Atlassian
description: Connect Jira and Confluence through Atlassian Rovo MCP.
permissionsText: API-token authentication requires organization-admin enablement and has narrower tool availability than OAuth.

steps: Ask your organization admin whether MCP API-token authentication is enabled.
Create a scoped API token and provide your account email.

name: Slack
description: Search Slack messages and read channel or thread context through Slack's hosted MCP server.
permissionsText: Uses Slack's hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server and an OAuth user token. Connect AI requests only public/private message search and channel/group history scopes; no message-writing scopes are requested.

steps: A server administrator must configure SLACK_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, SLACK_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, and SLACK_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI on the backend. Slack requires this callback to use HTTPS; for local development, point it at an HTTPS tunnel that forwards to the backend callback path /connect-ai/api/oauth/callback.
Register the exact SLACK_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI value in the Slack app's OAuth & Permissions > Redirect URLs and enable PKCE (S256). The OAuth request uses the Slack MCP resource https://mcp.slack.com.
The Slack app must be internal to your workspace or published in the Slack Marketplace to use Slack's official MCP server. Ask a workspace administrator to approve/install the app if required.

The sign-in requests these read-only user scopes: search:read.public, search:read.private, channels:history, groups:history. Successful authorization is followed by a real MCP handshake and tools/list discovery.

name: Notion
description: Notion's hosted MCP server uses a hosted OAuth consent flow.
permissionsText: Notion MCP is remotely hosted and consent-based. This server does not implement MCP OAuth protected-resource discovery or Notion's client authorization flow, so this connection cannot be completed here.
unavailableReason: Notion's hosted MCP requires an OAuth flow for this client. MCP OAuth discovery and authorization are not implemented in Connect AI, so there is no supported connection method yet.

steps: Use Notion MCP from a client listed in Notion's supported integrations, and have a workspace admin approve the client if MCP Governance is enabled.
Connect AI can enable this only after its server supports Notion's OAuth client/discovery protocol.

name: Splunk
description: Connect to a supported Splunk Enterprise or Cloud MCP endpoint.

fields.name: token
fields.label: Encrypted Splunk MCP token
fields.helpText: Generate this in the Splunk MCP Server app; ordinary Splunk platform tokens are not interchangeable.

permissionsText: Requires the Splunk MCP Server app and its own encrypted MCP token; a Splunk platform URL is not an MCP endpoint.

steps: An administrator installs and configures the Splunk MCP Server app and grants the mcp_tool_execute capability to your role.
In that app, generate an encrypted MCP token (requires edit_tokens_own and mcp_tool_admin for your own token) and copy its MCP endpoint.
Enter that exact endpoint and encrypted token. Do not disable TLS verification in production.

scopes: mcp_tool_execute; token creation requires edit_tokens_own and mcp_tool_admin

name: PagerDuty
description: Connect to PagerDuty's hosted remote MCP server.

fields.name: headerValue
fields.label: Authorization value
fields.helpText: PagerDuty accepts Token token=<API key> or Bearer <OAuth token>. This client supports the API-token header form.

permissionsText: PagerDuty's remote MCP endpoint accepts API-token or OAuth bearer authorization. This application supports the API-token header form and verifies it with a real MCP handshake.

steps: Create an API key with only the PagerDuty permissions needed for your investigations.
Use the hosted endpoint and enter the Authorization value as Token token=<your API key>.
Your PagerDuty administrator may need to approve MCP access for the account.

scopes: PagerDuty API permissions required by selected tools

name: Datadog
description: Connect to Datadog's hosted MCP server for your Datadog site.
permissionsText: The official remote MCP server supports OAuth or both DD_API_KEY and DD_APPLICATION_KEY headers. This application supports the header method; OAuth discovery is not implemented.

steps: Choose your Datadog site and copy the MCP endpoint from the official setup guide; the endpoint differs by site.
Create scoped API and application keys, preferably for a service account. Grant mcp_read and the resource read permissions your investigations need.
Enter the headers exactly as DD_API_KEY and DD_APPLICATION_KEY, then test the MCP connection.

scopes: mcp_read and underlying resource read permissions

name: Grafana
description: Connect to Grafana Cloud with OAuth, or use a service-account token with a self-hosted Grafana MCP server.

fields.name: grafanaUrl
fields.label: Grafana instance URL
fields.helpText: Base URL of your self-hosted Grafana instance. HTTPS is required except for explicitly enabled local/private development.

fields.name: token
fields.label: Grafana service-account token
fields.helpText: Sent only to the trusted Grafana MCP endpoint in X-Grafana-Service-Account-Token. Use least-privilege read permissions.

fields.name: endpointToken
fields.label: MCP endpoint bearer token (optional)
fields.placeholder: Only if your MCP endpoint requires it
fields.helpText: Separate from the Grafana token. Sent as Authorization: Bearer to the MCP endpoint.

permissionsText: Grafana Cloud uses the hosted https://mcp.grafana.com/mcp server with OAuth 2.1; authorize as your Grafana user and Connect AI discovers the tools available under your Grafana permissions. Self-hosted Grafana uses the open-source mcp-grafana server with a service-account token.

steps: Grafana Cloud: continue with Grafana Cloud sign-in. The hosted MCP server may ask for your stack URL if one is not included in the endpoint.

An administrator must register Connect AI under Grafana Assistant > Settings > Connectors > MCP clients and configure the generated client ID, secret, authorization URL, token URL, scopes, client-authentication method, and this app's exact callback in the backend environment. Use HTTPS in production; Grafana permits HTTP only for loopback development callbacks. OAuth uses PKCE S256.

Self-hosted: deploy the official Grafana MCP server using Streamable HTTP, enable --allow-grafana-url-override and an exact --allowed-grafana-urls allowlist, and configure --disable-write. Use a protected endpoint and least-privilege Grafana service-account token.

For self-hosted Grafana, enter the MCP endpoint URL, Grafana instance URL, and service-account token. If needed, enter a separate bearer token for the MCP endpoint. Credentials are encrypted by Connect AI.
The connection is reported as connected only after an authenticated MCP handshake and tool discovery.

scopes: Grafana OAuth scopes set by the registered client's Allowed access policy

name: Google Drive
description: Search and read files through Google's Drive MCP service.
permissionsText: Requests read-only Drive access. This Google service is a Developer Preview and requires Workspace Developer Preview membership and Google Cloud setup.

steps: A server administrator must enable Google Drive API and Google Drive MCP API, configure Google Auth Platform consent (Internal or External/test users), register https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file in Data Access, and join the Workspace Developer Preview Program.

Set GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET on the backend. Register this app's actual callback URI: http://localhost:8080/connect-ai/api/oauth/callback for local defaults, or the HTTPS value configured by CONNECTAI_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI in production.
The requested runtime scope is read-only drive.readonly; authorize the Drive access in the provider window. The backend then verifies MCP initialization and tool discovery.

name: Custom MCP server
description: Connect a supported MCP server using its endpoint and supported authentication.
permissionsText: Only Streamable HTTP is currently supported. Header names are validated and secret values are encrypted at rest.

steps: Get the MCP endpoint and authentication method from its owner.
Use an HTTPS endpoint outside local development.
Test the connection before saving.
